study.question: Can a label-free decoder calibrated exclusively on training history reconstruct native historical action IDs from the four supplied task masks, retaining the strongest visible model's native initialization and click AUC without using action values at inference?
study.hypothesis: The latest raw/mask common-nonzero treatments have identical aggregate metrics, as did the zero-start treatments. This suggests mask signatures may determine the relevant action partition, but does not prove eventwise invertibility. If each occupied signature has one native raw ID and validation introduces no unseen signatures, a train-calibrated mask decoder should reconstruct identical IDs and preserve the original native-initialization model trajectory. This directly tests whether the remaining native-vs-mask AUC gap is coding/initialization rather than additional inference information. Calibration uses raw training histories, so this cannot replace the existing strictly action-blind matched-initialization contrasts or establish total feedback dispensability.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines250-277 describes target-conditioned unnormalized history pooling. That inherited operation is unchanged. This is an input redundancy and native-row coding diagnostic, not a DIN reproduction or novel attention architecture.

Pinned source lines383-408 builds masks from action-token component membership; lines530-575 preserves history alignment and makes target action zero. It establishes the forward action-to-mask relation, not injectivity. No action_vocab contents are supplied to the candidate. We learn and audit a possible inverse using training inputs only.
Pinned forward123-170 uses per-task masks to initialize sequence hubs. No hub, broadcast or connectivity operator is adopted; this study audits feedback already carried by masks in the incumbent.
Pinned forward113-145 pools history before token interactions. No token interaction replacement is made; changing architecture would confound native coding attribution.
Pinned forward117-145 applies sparse filtering after history pooling. No filtering operator is adopted; sparsity is not tested by this information diagnostic.

study.proposed_difference: Append only34 int64 nonlearned decoder/telemetry entries (272 bytes) after inherited initialization. Four bits from named task masks index16 codebook slots. During train only, valid raw history IDs update per-signature min/max by deterministic integer reductions before prediction. At eval, all codebook state is immutable; unknown signatures use a fixed nonspecial row. Candidate replaces action IDs at train/eval; two matched controls isolate scaffolding and inference-only replacement. No vocabulary lookup, reinitialization, new learned parameter, label supervision for decoding, external I/O or extra data pass. Collisions are retained and reported, never silently interpreted as an inverse.
predictions: If the inverse hypothesis holds, every seen signature has min=max; training reconstruction error counter is zero; authorized host validation diagnostic finds zero unseen valid signatures and zero eventwise ID mismatches. These are prerequisites for an exact-redundancy claim.

Scaffolding bridge should reproduce the untouched utility reference. With identical decoded IDs, candidate and eval-only decoder should have identical parameter trajectories/predictions apart from measured execution nondeterminism. Original visible reference click AUC is0.6689610675617089; it is a prior measurement, not a new outcome.

Predeclare practical validation discrepancy as abs paired click AUC difference>0.0002. Smaller differences alone do not prove equivalence; require reconstruction diagnostics, all four AUC/Logloss values and, if host exposes paired predictions, max probability difference<=1e-7. Exact equality is the predicted stronger outcome when all IDs match.

All learned parameter counts should remain32192421. Decoder adds training integer reductions and evaluation mask bit assembly/gather; measure latency/throughput and allocated GPU/wall cost rather than assume efficiency.
falsifiers: Any valid training signature with min!=max falsifies a unique native-ID inverse on observed training data. Equality of aggregate metrics in earlier rounds would then require a weaker partition/optimization explanation.
Any validation signature unseen in training, or nonzero validation ID reconstruction error under a frozen map, falsifies exact recovery over that population. Do not refit from validation actions.

A scaffold-vs-untouched change reveals implementation/state/measurement effects and blocks attributing candidate differences to information. A decoder-vs-bridge AUC loss>0.0002 despite verified ID parity points to a numerical or implementation discrepancy, not evidence of new action information.

If online and eval-only decoders diverge, investigate coverage/collisions and training substitutions before claiming conditional redundancy. Passing this diagnostic does not establish repeated-seed or production-time validity.
alternative_explanations: Multiple raw action tokens may share a four-bit mask signature, despite equal prior AUC/Logloss; native random row distinctions could matter within a signature.
Native initialization sensitivity or row assignment, rather than information, can explain earlier canonical/affine mask gaps.
Online mapping may change when another native ID appears; rare unseen validation signatures trigger the preregistered fallback.
Frozen-seed replays are not independent repetitions; equal aggregate metrics need not imply equal per-example predictions.
Extra reduction kernels, in-place nonlearned state, checkpoint handling or sparse optimizer nondeterminism could affect costs or execution. Host tensor checks remain necessary.
Masks still carry historical feedback; this cannot identify total feedback utility or point-in-time availability under the inherited offline policy.
